Fixes #32775 ### Description This PR adds support for `HTTP\0.9` in `HttpProtocol`. ### Behaviour before the fix Request ```GET /``` Response ```*Connection closed``` Logs ``` fail: ... System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: Version doesn't map to a known HTTP protocol. (Parameter 'version') at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpProtocol.GetHttpProtocol(Version version) in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Abstractions.dll:token 0x6000106+0x8b at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.IIS.Core.IISHttpContext.Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Features.IHttpRequestFeature.get_Protocol() in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.IIS.dll:token 0x600033c+0x0... ``` ### Behaviour after the fix Request ``` GET /``` Response ``` Bad Request

Bad Request - Invalid Hostname

HTTP Error 400. The request hostname is invalid.

*Connection closed ``` Logs ``` info: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics[1] Request starting HTTP/0.9 GET http:/// - - info: Microsoft.AspNetCore.HostFiltering.HostFilteringMiddleware[3] HTTP/0.9 request rejected due to missing or empty host header. info: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics[2] Request finished HTTP/0.9 GET http:/// - - - 400 334 text/html 3.2967ms ```

issue_context.title: GetHttpProtocol support for 0.9
issue_context.body:
```
Exception:
System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: Version doesn't map to a known HTTP protocol. (Parameter 'version')
at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpProtocol.GetHttpProtocol(Version version)
at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.IIS.Core.IISHttpContext.Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Features.IHttpRequestFeature.get_Protocol()
at Microsoft.AspNetCore.HostFiltering.HostFilteringMiddleware.IsEmptyHostAllowed(HttpContext context)
at Microsoft.AspNetCore.HostFiltering.HostFilteringMiddleware.Invoke(HttpContext context)
at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.IIS.Core.IISHttpContextOfT`1.ProcessRequestAsync()
```

The default builder adds the HostFitleringMiddleware:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/52eff90fbcfca39b7eb58baad597df6a99a542b0/src/DefaultBuilder/src/WebHost.cs#L245

HTTP 0.9 doesn't set a Host, so it ends up here:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/dc5e11abdb05b322f4b74b3afbcfb352fe984b2e/src/Middleware/HostFiltering/src/HostFilteringMiddleware.cs#L191-L202

IIS uses GetHttpProtocol to get the string value:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/52eff90fbcfca39b7eb58baad597df6a99a542b0/src/Servers/IIS/IIS/src/Core/IISHttpContext.FeatureCollection.cs#L108-L110

Http.Sys would also be affected:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/52eff90fbcfca39b7eb58baad597df6a99a542b0/src/Servers/HttpSys/src/RequestProcessing/RequestContext.FeatureCollection.cs#L191

GetHttpProtocol doesn't support 0.9:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/fdabaf00a6720d852ec3120b7bbe4b14de2f3ccf/src/Http/Http.Abstractions/src/HttpProtocol.cs#L99-L106

Reported by a large internal partner.
comments:
If you do consider supporting it (oh lord, why?) you're going to have a bunch of validation work to do which may end up cross cutting between places;

- Request nature: single-line (method + path for requested document)
- Methods supported: GET only
- Response type: hypertext only
- Connection nature: terminated immediately after the response
- No HTTP headers (cannot transfer other content type files), No status/error codes, No URLs, No versioning
I don't know that we'd explicitly support it, but we'd like the failure to happen somewhere else 😁.
Note this was a regression between 3.1 and 5.0.
Triage: Add 0.9 to HttpProtocol list and verify that it's rejected by the host filtering middleware.

Thanks for contacting us.

We're moving this issue to the `Next sprint planning` milestone for future evaluation / consideration. We would like to keep this around to collect more feedback, which can help us with prioritizing this work. We will re-evaluate this issue, during our next planning meeting(s). 
If we later determine, that the issue has no community involvement, or it's very rare and low-impact issue, we will close it - so that the team can focus on more important and high impact issues.
To learn more about what to expect next and how this issue will be handled you can read more about our triage process [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/docs/TriageProcess.md).

> I don't know that we'd explicitly support it, but we'd like the failure to happen somewhere else

To be clear, we're not saying we support 0.9, but we would prefer a 400 failure from another middleware (like host filtering) or something else instead of a 500 like it gets now.
Hi, I would like to take this one

> Triage: Add 0.9 to HttpProtocol list and verify that it's rejected by the host filtering middleware.

I couldn't find an easy way to verify HTTP\0.9 is rejected in host filtering middleware.
In [HostFilteringMiddlewareTests](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Middleware/HostFiltering/test/HostFilteringMiddlewareTests.cs) `TestServer` is used and it is not calling `HttpProtocol.GetHttpProtocol(...)`

It looks like some options are:
- Call `HttpProtocol.IsHttp09` in `HostFilteringMiddleware` class and if `true` return 400 the same way as for host validation
- Create functional tests for `HttpSys` and `IIS` servers (HttpClient used in functional tests throws if HTTP\0.9 is used, so I will look for some other ways to test it)
- Change [RequestFeature](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/be21fc12bfde2fa7eab87bff5607d3bfa79a5ccf/src/Hosting/TestHost/src/RequestFeature.cs#L35) in `TestServer` so it uses `HttpProtocol.GetHttpProtocol(...)` when property `Protocol` is used
- Some other option

Could you please guide me here?
HostFilteringMiddleware would refuse the 0.9 request because it doesn't have a Host header. You can verify that manually with an application, it doesn't need to be automated.

review_comments:
Just as thought: don't add `Http09` here, but throw a `ProtocolNotSupportedException`, so that this exception can be handled upstreams with a concise message why the request is failing.

With the current state it looks like HTTP/0.9 is supported, which it actually isn't at all.

>looks like HTTP/0.9 is supported

Good point, we have several cases here:
1. `IIS` inproc hosting actually supports `HTTP\0.9`. If `HostFilteringMiddleware` is not used, you will get content.
2.  If `HostFilteringMiddleware` is used, it returns host validation failed HTML response (without status code in the first line as in `HTTP/1.0` or higher)
2. `Kestrel` doesn't support it and returns `HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request`

I agree field `Http09` can be misleading. Maybe put extra notes in the comment?

I don't think we can throw. It is a regression and before regression `HTTP\0.9` was parsed successfully.

Thanks for your points!

> Maybe put extra notes in the comment?

That would make it more obvious (for the future).
